lessons.heading: Who was Chanakya?
lessons.body:
*SAMPLE text for testing. Not reviewed.*

Chanakya, also known as Kautilya or Vishnugupta, is remembered as a teacher and royal adviser in ancient India, in the 4th century BCE. Tradition says he taught at Taxila and helped a young Chandragupta Maurya overthrow the Nanda dynasty of Magadha, founding the Maurya Empire around 322 BCE.

His name is attached to the *Arthashastra*, a long Sanskrit work on running a state. It covers taxes, law, the duties of a king, spies, diplomacy and war, in a practical and often blunt way.

## History and legend

Much of what we know about Chanakya comes from stories written down centuries later, and they do not always agree. Historians also debate when the Arthashastra was written and whether one person wrote all of it. In this title, traditional stories are labelled as tradition.

- Lived: about 375 to 283 BCE (traditional dates)
- Known for: the Arthashastra and advising Chandragupta Maurya
